introHeading: Wedding photo booths for The Bronx's biggest celebrations
introParas: Bronx weddings tend to run big and multigenerational — waterfront catering halls in Throggs Neck built for two-hundred-plus guests, receptions held near Pelham Bay Park right after a ceremony in the park, and estate-style properties in Riverdale where the ceremony and reception happen on the same grounds. We plan every Bronx booking around that guest count from the start, because a booth that keeps up fine at eighty guests can bottleneck fast at twice that size.

The mirror booth remains the safest choice for most Bronx receptions — full-length format, works for the flower girl and the grandparents alike, which matters at the family-heavy guest lists common across the borough. Past roughly 150 guests, routine at Throggs Neck's bigger halls, we usually pair it with a roaming attendant so seated tables get covered directly instead of everyone funneling into one line. For a younger Mott Haven crowd who wants the clip posted before the band's second set, the 360 booth tends to see the heaviest use.

On logistics: we carry a $3 million policy and turn a certificate of insurance around the same day you give us your venue's contact — standard for the catering halls that host most Bronx weddings. We arrive an hour ahead and set up in about 20 minutes, in a 10ft x 10ft footprint where the room allows it or 8ft x 8ft with 7.5ft of clearance where it's tighter, plus a dedicated outlet that isn't sharing a circuit with the DJ or kitchen. The Bronx is a standard service area with no surprise travel fee — we quote it from your venue's ZIP code before you book.

faqHeading: Wedding Photo Booth in The Bronx — FAQ

faqs.q: How many hours should we book for a Bronx wedding?
faqs.a: Three to four hours covers most receptions, though larger Throggs Neck catering hall weddings sometimes run longer. Send us your guest count and run sheet and we'll suggest a start time and whether a second attendant makes sense before we quote you extra hours.

faqs.q: Our guest list is large — can one booth keep up?
faqs.a: Past about 150 guests, which is common at Bronx catering halls, we usually suggest pairing your static booth with a roaming attendant. That way seated tables get covered directly instead of everyone lining up at one station all night.

faqs.q: Do you charge a travel fee in The Bronx?
faqs.a: No surprise fees. The Bronx is a standard service area and we quote any travel cost from your venue's ZIP code before you book — Riverdale, Throggs Neck, Pelham Bay, Mott Haven and Country Club are all regular territory for us.

faqs.q: Which booth works best for a Bronx wedding?
faqs.a: The mirror booth is the safest choice for the family-heavy, multigenerational guest lists common at Bronx receptions. For a younger Mott Haven crowd, the 360 booth gets used the hardest.

faqs.q: How much space and power does the booth need?
faqs.a: Optimal is a 10ft x 10ft footprint, with 8ft x 8ft and 7.5ft of ceiling clearance as the minimum. We also need a standard 110V outlet within 15 feet — many Bronx catering halls run tight circuits for the DJ and kitchen, so we bring our own dedicated run.

About 20 minutes once we're in the room. We build in a full hour ahead of your scheduled start so everything is tested before your first guest walks in. If you need us on site earlier than that, idle time is $150 per hour.

faqs.q: Can you send our venue a certificate of insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. We carry a $3 million policy and turn COIs around the same day you send us your venue's contact — standard practice for the catering halls most Bronx weddings are held at.

faqs.q: Do we get every photo from the night, not just the prints?
faqs.a: Yes. Every image lands in an online gallery you can download in full and share with guests, on top of the unlimited prints handed out on the night.

faqs.q: Our catering hall has another wedding right before ours — how does load-in work?
faqs.a: We coordinate directly with the hall's event coordinator to find a load-in window that doesn't conflict with the event ahead of yours. Throggs Neck's waterfront halls especially tend to run tight Saturday turnovers, so we confirm timing before the day rather than showing up and hoping.

faqs.q: How will out-of-town guests get to our Bronx venue without a car?
faqs.a: It depends on the neighborhood — Riverdale has a Metro-North Hudson Line stop, Pelham Bay sits at the 6 train's northern terminus, and Throggs Neck and Country Club are best reached by car or bus since neither has a direct subway line. Tell us your venue and we can usually confirm the nearest stop for your invitations.
